A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same KGE-MOS research, despite the title changing from Knowledge Graph Completion to Knowledge Graph Embeddings. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables and complete Appendices A–F support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original link-prediction experiments on four datasets, a mixture-size ablation and computational timing measurements.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds comparator results, WN18RR evaluation, empirical rank measurements and a higher-dimensional experiment.

M1.justification: The mixture of softmaxes, learned mixture weights, shared entity embeddings, two-layer projections, entropy regularization and inverse-relation inference remain unchanged. Applying this existing output layer to ComplEx and CompGCN does not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: V2 adds actual evaluation on WN18RR, a lower-connectivity graph, in Appendix F.1 and Table 13. All four original datasets and the subject/object link-prediction tasks remain, making this a limited extension of dataset coverage.

E2.justification: Table 2 expands the evaluated base models from DistMult, RESCAL and ConvE to include ComplEx and CompGCN, each compared with its KGE-MOS variant. These additions substantially broaden the comparisons to another bilinear model and a graph-convolutional encoder; their earlier background mentions were not evaluations.

E3.justification: V2 adds a d=5000 experiment with batch size 200 and specifies matched ComplEx bottlenecks and dataset-dependent CompGCN dimensions. Appendix F.3 also revises the reported RESCAL/RESCAL-MOS batch-size exceptions. Existing filtered metrics, epoch budget and stopping rules remain; the PDFs do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained mixture-size ablation, Appendix F.4.2 directly examines learned log-probability matrix ranks to test bottleneck removal. Appendix F.4.4 adds a K=1 versus K=4 comparison at d=5000 to investigate when mixing stops helping. These substantially extend the mechanism and sensitivity analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions describe three initialization runs, report benchmark and mixture-ablation standard deviations, and use paired Wilcoxon tests at p<0.05. Expanded benchmark rows reuse these practices. No increased run count or new statistical procedure is established; uncertainty for the new d=5000 results is unspecified.

E6.justification: V2 adds ComplEx/CompGCN, WN18RR, empirical-rank and d=5000 results, and updates Table 2 aggregate deltas. Newly reported WN18RR MRRs include 0.421 for DistMult versus 0.129 for DistMult-MOS at d=200. The 48 original detailed benchmark rows, mixture ablation and timings remain unchanged. New CompGCN-MOS openbiolink scores disagree between Tables 2 and 12.

T1.justification: The proof of Proposition 3.1 corrects the adjacency reconstruction factor from 1/τ+ to 1/(τ+−τ−). The rank-bottleneck theorems and sufficient maximum-out-degree bound remain unchanged. Moving proofs to Appendix B and simplifying notation do not constitute additional theoretical results.

C1.justification: V1 broadly claims improved performance and distributional fidelity across its experiments. V2 explicitly confines the practical improvement claims in the abstract and conclusion to large graphs. The central rank-bottleneck analysis, connectivity bound and KGE-MOS contribution remain.

C2.justification: V2 introduces possible overfitting as an explanation for weak small-dataset results and interprets the d=5000 experiment as reduced bottleneck impact combined with memory-driven batch-size costs. It also expands discussion of entity ordering and applicability boundaries. The batch-size causal explanation is not isolated by the experiment.

D1.justification: Appendix F.3 adds CompGCN implementation information, including initial dimensions, a single GCN layer, composition choice, omitted bias/basis decomposition and dropout. V2 also documents WN18RR splits and the higher-dimensional experiment's memory constraint. Existing KGE-MOS hyperparameters, hardware and code-access information remain.

R1.justification: Sections 2.1, 7 and Appendix D.1 extend discussion to language-model encoders, CompGCN, ExpressivE and graph/path-based reasoning, with corresponding citations and scope qualifications. The primary novelty claim and relationship to earlier language-model mixture-of-softmaxes work remain unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 substantially condenses and rewrites the introduction and model overview, moves the Section 3 proofs and detailed exposition into appendices, and reorganizes Appendix F.4 into four subsections. It also changes the title terminology, author information and citation style.

P2.justification: V2 adds a prediction-task diagram and empirical-rank, higher-dimensional and WN18RR tables. Existing comparison tables gain model rows, dimension footnotes and highlighting. The document adopts a different visual template, heading treatment and caption emphasis; earlier figures are retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: V2 better supports the unchanged method through broader comparisons, WN18RR negative results and direct rank measurements, while correcting Proposition 3.1 and narrowing performance claims. These gains are tempered by the confounded dimension/batch-size experiment and a new reporting inconsistency: CompGCN-MOS on openbiolink has NLL/MRR 5.43/0.274 in Table 2 but 5.35/0.278 in Table 12.
